summary.headline: PTC India Q4 FY26 standalone volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 BU, but PAT fell 85% to ₹75.7 crore on the prior-year PEL sale gain.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone trading volume rose 24% YoY to 23.6 billion units, and FY26 volume grew 12% to 92.8 BU. Reported profit fell sharply because Q4 FY25 included the PEL (PTC Energy) sale gain of about ₹521 crore; excluding it, standalone PAT rose 18% to ₹75.74 crore for the quarter and was flat at ₹397 crore for the year. Management said the DISCOM liquidity surplus cut rebate and surcharge income (rebate fell from ₹121 crore to ₹97 crore), so operating income held near ₹450 crore for the year. The board has lifted its pause on the PFS divestment, with the route and advisers still to be decided by a board committee.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 down from ₹17.6; FY26 down from ₹28.88
Around ₹2,400 crore as of call date (approx.)

segments.name: Short-term / exchange trading
segments.commentary: Now about 56% of business by management's account, up from the 50:50 target mix, driving most of the Q4 volume growth. Competes with more than 70 licensed traders.

segments.name: Cross-border and long-term trading
segments.commentary: Management describes a niche edge here with only about 4-6 credible competitors. Cross-border is one of three cited moats alongside balance sheet and relationships.

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: 68 lakh certificates delivered in FY26 to cover balance renewable obligations. The company also trades power for Himachal Pradesh from 14 hydro projects.

segments.name: Consultancy and new initiatives
segments.commentary: Includes PM KUSUM smart meter and rooftop solar work, an ADB project for Laos, Thailand and Cambodia, and BESS power trading. Green power supply to GAIL Vijaipur green hydrogen (10 MW) is also in place.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth expected to track or slightly exceed national power demand growth of about 5% a year.
Trading margins guided flat, with movement of only plus or minus a few basis points; growth to come from volume rather than margin.
Medium- and short-term contracts expected to take a larger share; long-term contracts may shrink to 10-12 years from 25.
PFS divestment process restarted after the board lifted its pause; a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months, with material developments to be disclosed.
NLC India JV: about 2,000 MW initial hydro/renewable portfolio, subject to DIPAM-level government approval.
Teesta Urja: cofferdam phase to supply about 40-50% of capacity by September or October 2026; full dam completion targeted for 2029.
capex_capacity: Net cash about ₹2,800 crore at 31 March 2026, around ₹2,400 crore on the call date, per management.
Cash is held for working capital needs (the business is cyclical), a strategic 'war chest' for small, value-adding investments, and returns to shareholders.
NLC India JV: MoU for about 2,000 MW initially; may go higher or lower depending on government permissions.
Teesta Urja hydro: cofferdam phase first, full dam later.
PFS divestment proceeds would be reinvested in trading-adjacent opportunities; management said no fixed return benchmark will be applied.
demand_pricing: Management reported record peak demand of about 260 GW the previous day; electricity demand is growing about 5% a year.
Renewables reached about 26% of energy consumed, against a 29% government target for the year.
Competition is intense on exchange and short-term trades, with over 70 licensed traders. Margins are under pressure; management says trading margin growth is difficult.
Customer base is more than 800 consumers. Data centres and green hydrogen are emerging demand segments.
Rebate and surcharge income fell as DISCOM payments became timely, reducing income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT contribution from the PEL sale and how will it affect future earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: The PEL sale produced a PBT gain of about ₹521 crore in the prior year, and PAT from PEL was about ₹33 crore in FY25. FY26 numbers have no PEL profit and are a good base for trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth do you expect over the next 2-3 years, and is PFS divestment still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is expected at about 5%, slightly above national growth. The board's pause on PFS divestment has been lifted, and a board committee will decide the structure over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition, and does it pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is strong on exchange trades (over 70 traders) and limited in long-term and cross-border trades (about 4-6 players). Growth will come from volume, not margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance be deployed, and what is the return hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is kept for cyclical working capital, strategic investments that add value to the core business, and returns to shareholders. Management said it would not hold the company to a fixed ROCE or IRR benchmark that delays value realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline across long-, medium- and short-term contracts, and how are spreads moving?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term contracts are harder to win, with more focus on medium- and short-term deals. Spreads are not expected to rise much or fall much, with margin changes of plus or minus a few basis points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NLC JV plans, capex and timing, and what is net cash and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: NLC JV targets about 2,000 MW initially, awaiting DIPAM approval, with no timeline. Net cash is about ₹2,800 crore at March-end and about ₹2,400 crore now. Management said distressed assets were largely resolved and remaining ones are expected to be resolved in the near term.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from competition, with management saying margins will stay roughly flat in the next 2-3 years.
Reliance on short-term exchange trades, which raises volume volatility and reduces contract visibility.
Lower rebate and surcharge income as DISCOM payments improve; this has already cut income.
PFS divestment timing, route and value, with no investment banker yet announced.
Capital allocation of a large cash balance (about ₹2,400-2,800 crore) without a stated return target.
Asset quality of the remaining financing book, which management would not detail.
NLC JV and Teesta Urja timelines depend on government approvals and construction schedules.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and franchise moats, but cautious on margins and evasive on PFS divestment details, asset quality and capital deployment. Management repeatedly deferred specifics to future disclosures.
key_quotes: Margins we don't expect to grow substantially. Marginal, you know, decimal percentage is plus and minus.
So if many people enter into this space and I think many people have entered but then their volumes speak for themselves.
Now we have to report now that that particular decision to pause is not there.
